message.reasoning:
We need to generate a test class covering the test cases in JSON. The existing test class already covers some cases (simple walk with mock). We need to expand to cover all groups: valid input with validation enabled/disabled, invalid JSON, null executionContext, unsupported InputFormat, OutputFormat throws exception, empty JSON object, JSON literal null, JSON array, whitespace only input, null input string, null outputFormat, outputFormat returns null, executionContext with customizer (no effect), null InputFormat, empty string input.

We need to use JUnit5, Mockito. For SimpleStringOutputFormat, ThrowingOutputFormat, NullReturningOutputFormat we need to define simple implementations within test class (or as static inner classes). Also need to handle exceptions.

The method under test: JsonSchema.walk(ExecutionContext, String, InputFormat, OutputFormat<T>, boolean). It returns T from OutputFormat.apply(Set<ValidationMessage>). So we can mock OutputFormat or use real implementation.

Simplify: For most tests we can use mock OutputFormat that returns a string "Validation succeeded". For exception tests we need a custom OutputFormat that throws.

For unsupported InputFormat: we need to assume InputFormat.YAML is not supported; calling walk should throw UnsupportedOperationException from deserialize. We'll just call and assertThrows.

For null ExecutionContext: the method may create default context; we just pass null and expect success.

For null OutputFormat: should throw NullPointerException. We'll assertThrows.

For null InputFormat: same.

For whitespace only, empty string, null input string: expect JsonProcessingException (Jackson). We'll assertThrows.

For null input string as literal null (the JSON literal "null"): that's a string "null". That's valid JSON, returns success.

Implementation details: Need to create JsonSchemaFactory instance. Use simple schema that accepts any type: maybe "{}" or {"type":"object"}? For array case need schema that permits arrays; using "{}" (no constraints) might accept any JSON. Use "{}". But earlier they used SIMPLE_SCHEMA = "{ \"type\": \"object\" }". That would reject array? Possibly validation would fail but OutputFormat still called? The walk method will still call outputFormat.apply with validation messages; if validation fails, messages will be non-empty but outputFormat still called. For simplicity, we can use "{}" schema which allows anything.

Let's define SCHEMA = "{}". Use factory.getSchema(SCHEMA).

Define SimpleStringOutputFormat implements OutputFormat<String> with apply returning "Validation succeeded" (or "Validation skipped").

Define ThrowingOutputFormat implements OutputFormat<String> with apply throwing RuntimeException.

Define NullReturningOutputFormat implements OutputFormat<String> returning null.

We also need ExecutionContext class; we can instantiate new ExecutionContext().

Now test methods: Use @ParameterizedTest with MethodSource for groups? Could create separate test methods per group.

But requirement: one test function per test case group, ensuring all cases are covered. So each group will have its own test method, maybe parameterized for multiple cases if needed. Most groups have single case.

Implement test methods:

- testValidInputValidationEnabled
- testValidInputValidationDisabled
- testInvalidJsonInput
- testNullExecutionContext
- testUnsupportedInputFormat
- testOutputFormatThrowsException
- testEmptyJsonObjectValidationEnabled
- testJsonLiteralNullValidationEnabled
- testJsonArrayInputValidationEnabled
- testWhitespaceOnlyInput
- testNullInputString
- testNullOutputFormat
- testOutputFormatReturnsNull
- testExecutionContextWithCustomizerNoEffect (we can just pass a custom ExecutionContext with some config, but still expect success)
- testNullInputFormat
- testEmptyStringInput

Define helper method to create schema and output format.

For tests expecting success, we verify result equals "Validation succeeded" (or "Validation skipped" for disabled). For disabled case we can have SimpleStringOutputFormat returning "Validation skipped". Or we can use same format and just check result.

Implementation: In each test, set up schema and executionContext (or null). Use outputFormat (mock or custom). For mocking we can just use mock as earlier.

But for simplicity, use custom SimpleStringOutputFormat.

Define static class SimpleStringOutputFormat<T> implements OutputFormat<T> { private final T result; public SimpleStringOutputFormat(T result){ this.result=result; } @Override public T apply(Set<ValidationMessage> messages){ return result; } }

Now test.

Need imports: org.junit.jupiter.api.*, org.junit.jupiter.params.*, org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.*, static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*, com.networknt.schema.*, com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonProcessingException, java.util.Set, java.util.Collections.

Now write test class.

Edge: InputFormat.YAML may exist; we assume not supported; calling walk will cause UnsupportedOperationException. We'll assertThrows.

For null InputFormat, same.

For null outputFormat, calling walk will cause NullPointerException when trying to call apply. So assertThrows NullPointerException.

For whitespace only, deserialize will throw JsonProcessingException. So assertThrows JsonProcessingException.

Similarly for empty string.

For null input string (value null), we pass null, expect NullPointerException.

For null executionContext, pass null; expecting success.

Now produce final code.
